facts.text: Nahcotta was named after Chief Nahcati, a local Chinook leader who lived along the western shore of Shoalwater Bay.
The town’s first post office opened in 1889 and operated until February 27, 2021, when it closed after funding was denied.
A narrow‑gauge railroad ran from Ilwaco up the Long Beach Peninsula to Nahcotta, reaching the town in 1889 and operating until 1930.
In the late 1800s, settlers built a few homes and businesses where Nahcotta now stands, but most gathered in nearby Oysterville for work.
The area that became Nahcotta was once a thriving oyster‑harvesting hub, with ships docking at Shoalwater Bay’s channel close to the town’s future site.
Nahcotta sits on Willapa Bay, on the eastern coast of the Long Beach Peninsula, within the Ocean Park census‑designated place.
